content.title: Tottenham vs Nottingham Forest: 0-3 and key stats
content.text: Tottenham Hotspur fell 3-0 to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The visitors scored on the stroke of halftime and twice after the break to seal a statement away win. Spurs had plenty of the ball and chances, but Forest were far more efficient in front of goal. Big moments Forest struck first at 45 minutes. Neco Williams delivered a deep cross and Igor Jesus met it with a firm header past Guglielmo Vicario. That set the tone. After halftime, Callum Hudson-Odoi carried and slipped a pass for Morgan Gibbs-White, who finished with his right foot in the 62nd minute. Late on, Williams crossed again and substitute Taiwo Awoniyi guided in the third at 87 minutes. Yellow cards arrived for Ibrahim Sangaré (53) and Awoniyi (88) for Forest, while Destiny Udogie saw yellow for Spurs (82). Michael Oliver refereed. What the stats say Tottenham had 58 percent possession and out-shot Forest 14 to 8. The difference came in accuracy. Spurs put only 3 shots on target, Forest hit 7. Expected goals favored the visitors 1.48 to 1.14. Spurs created 4 big chances but scored none and even hit the woodwork through Kevin Danso. Forest created 3 big chances and scored 2. The home side also racked up 13 corners to Forest’s 3. Clearances tell another story: Forest 40, Spurs 12. When it mattered, Matz Sels saved 3 shots and prevented 1.58 goals, while Vicario finished at -0.45 goals prevented. Standout performers by Sofascore Rating Neco Williams earned a Sofascore Rating of 8 with two assists, two shots on target and two key passes. His crossing decided the game. Nikola Milenković also posted 8, stacking up 11 clearances and 3 blocks. Behind them, Matz Sels landed 7.8 with three saves and smart positioning all afternoon. Morgan Gibbs-White scored and posted a 7.5, while Igor Jesus added a 7.4 with his first-half header. Taiwo Awoniyi came on to score and finished at 7. For Spurs, Cristian Romero and Dominic Solanke led the way at 7.1, with Vicario on 7 after four saves. On Sofascore, 10 is a perfect Rating. How the game unfolded Igor Tudor’s Tottenham lined up 4-4-2 and made two halftime changes, bringing on Destiny Udogie and Lucas Bergvall. Later, Richarlison and Mathys Tel went off on 67 minutes, with Xavi Simons and Randal Kolo Muani introduced. Tel’s exit was injury-related. Vitor Pereira’s Forest set up in a 4-2-3-1. Hudson-Odoi made way for Ryan Yates on 70 minutes, then Igor Jesus for Awoniyi on 71. Dan Ndoye joined late, and Nicolás Domínguez and James McAtee came on in stoppage time to see it out. Spurs fans will feel the volume was there but the finish was not. Forest fans will enjoy a clean, clinical away performance.
